subject: general
question: A circle touches the side BC of triangle ABC at P. Side AB and AC are produced to touch the circle at points Q and R respectively. The length of AQ is:
solution:
**Concept:**

Length of sides of a triangle drawn from an external point to a circle are equal 

Two tangents are equal in length drawn from the same origin point. 

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9630eb2ab9ada6f50522fb31f71d1b08e1dd8d3849609745c6b37732e8bba29e.png] 

AQ = AR, BQ = BP, CP = CR ∵ [Tangents from the same origin point] 

Perimeter of triangle ABC = AB + BC + AC 

⇒ AB + (BP + PC) + (AR - CR)

⇒ (AB + BQ) + PC + (AQ - PC)

⇒ AQ + AQ 

⇒ 2 AQ 

**∴ AQ = 1/2 × (AB + BC + AC)**

15
